correctness.rationale: For a loop-chain of length \(r=2m-1\) on \(n\) vertices there are exactly \(n-1\) forward labels and therefore \(r-(n-1)\) loops. If one vertex had three loops, two loop labels would have the same parity; transposing those two labels is a nonidentity parity-preserving permutation and leaves the entire matrix-unit product unchanged because both factors equal the same \(E_{s,s}\). Parity isolation therefore gives at most two loops per vertex, hence \(r-(n-1)\le2n\), equivalently \(n\ge\lceil2m/3\rceil\). The focal construction has \(v_k=1+\lfloor k/3\rfloor\), reaches exactly \(\lceil2m/3\rceil\) vertices, and the source proves its required uniqueness property.

value.rationale: The focal source explicitly leaves the optimal finite matrix level open. The result isolates a sharp obstruction for the exact extraction mechanism used there: the factor \(2/3\) cannot be improved by a denser packing of loops into the same path architecture. This is a motivated structural boundary, not an arbitrary parameter slice, because it identifies what must change in any attempt to lower the level: one must leave the single-entry loop-chain parity-isolation mechanism rather than merely rearrange it.
